content:
maria: heads-up — seeing steady memory drip on ded-1 when requests have longctx > 32k. tenant=t-hyperspike keeps growing KV residency and we start paging other tenants.

josh: i noticed this after the 23:45 deploy, same cluster. on one GPU kv_ram went +18% over ~30m, didn’t recover between requests.

andrea: do you have a quick profile/snippet? is this CUDA pinned alloc churn or GPU<->CPU page transfers?

maria: throwing a snippet i grabbed from the logs and lightweight profiler:
```
# sample kv residency snapshot (30m window)
# tenant, residency_pct, avg_page_lifetime_s, page_fragments
t-hyperspike   72%   42s   114
t-smallshop     6%   12s    9
free_pool      22%
fragmentation_ratio ~0.41
```

josh: that fragmentation_ratio is the smoking gun imo — many small fragments from longctx reuse not being consolidated. eviction prefers LRU pages but doesn’t compact fragments, so free_pool is noisy.

rachel: that matches the telemetry we started adding last month: per-page allocation units are counted but we don’t account for subpage fragmentation when enforcing per-tenant quotas. tenant can accumulate many subpage fragments and still look "under quota" by our coarse count.

ben: possible mitigations off top:
- soft watermarks per-tenant (warn/slow-path) at 60/75/90%
- compaction pass when free_pool < 25% or fragmentation_ratio > 0.35
- early eviction of pages with last_access > 30s for tenants above soft watermark

andrea: compaction will cost async memcpy and compute; schedule on low-GPU-load windows. also consider making compaction incremental (merge N fragments per pass) to avoid 100ms spikes.

maria: proposed experiment plan:
1) enable soft watermark + early eviction for heavy tenants (flag: kv.eviction.soft=true)
2) run a lightweight incremental compaction during idle (kv.compaction.mode=incremental)
3) add `kv.reuse_ratio` diagnostic tag on requests to measure how often a request hits an existing page vs alloc

josh: started a canary: setting kv/compaction=incremental on ded-1 region for 30m (canary id c-231).

deploy-bot: canary c-231: kv/compaction=incremental rolled to 2/3 nodes in ded-1 at 1798888205.

sre-bot: alert at 1798888220: ded-1 free_pool below threshold (20%) — triggered eviction sweep (policy=soft+aggressive).

andrea: any p99 perf regressions observed during the canary? compaction could add tail latency if run inline.

josh: quick numbers: normal tenants p50/p95 stable. t-hyperspike p99 increased ~12% during compaction windows; we also saw short CUDA memcpy stalls correlated with compaction passes. p99 spike ~40ms additional on those tail requests.

rachel: suggests compaction was blocking or not overlapping copies correctly. use cudaMemcpyAsync + stream fences so compute can overlap with copies. also try compaction slices of <8ms to avoid long stalls.

maria: updated plan: run three experiments A/B/C:
A) soft-watermark eviction only (no compaction)
B) incremental compaction but strictly async copies + very small slice budget (<=8ms)
C) per-tenant token-budget gating to cap how fast a tenant can accumulate new KV pages (rate limit allocs)

ben: I'll draft the PR with feature flags, telemetry counters (kv.fragmentation_ratio, kv.page_reuse_rate, kv.alloc_rate_per_tenant) and a debug endpoint `/debug/kv/residency` to snapshot state.

maria: tagging @andrea for kernel-level advice on async copy patterns and @josh for rollout coordinates.

josh: one more thought: we should also track `avg_page_reuse` per request type (generation vs chat) — long contexts with low reuse are prime candidates for early eviction policy.

andrea: agreed. we can add a lightweight counter in runtime that increments on cache hit and attach to request metadata. low-overhead.

maria: done. filing follow-up INF-4302 with experiment matrix + sample logs. if anyone sees new longctx tenants causing spikes, ping me in this thread or @maria.

ben: PR sketch incoming, will include telemetry dashboards and alert thresholds.

maria: thanks all — will post results after 24h of canary runs. :thumbsup:
